verdicts.how: Re-fetched schema_troy.ron from raw.githubusercontent.com (2026-11-10T20:57:37Z, HTTP 200, 6,752,098 bytes, SHA-256 8332875a61825d0c67516ccbd155ab9c38c52f628e1ab664f91074cfbffa45e5, byte-identical to the finder's copy) and parsed it with the checker's own scripts (work-check/scripts/parse.py, tabledef.py, quotes.py). _kv_morale_tables lookup (line 158187) holds 129 key/description pairs, every one with a description; the checker read all 129; each quoted pair occurs exactly once; the table definition (line 199) has only key StringU8 and value F32.
verdicts.note: Verified by reading every key: none names entering a battle, deployment, the battle's start, time spent in battle or a loss-independent drain; apart from morale_base the only unconditional side-wide terms are the eight difficulty modifiers. The naval morale list (69 keys, line 158192, not cited by the finder) has none either. 'Moving toward the computed one each tick' is a fair reading of 'The ideal changed morale amount' and the minimum per-tick change, not a stated formula. Caveats hold: no value is in the file; 'warcry_effect_range' is described 'NOT USED', so a defined key need not be active; the descriptions' source and faithfulness are INFERRED (CODE label accepted on that basis). Checker observation (CODE, sibling): WARHAMMER II and III define 'autoresolver_minimum_morale_loss' ('Minimum morale loss in one autoresolver combat round') and '_per_second', a loss-independent morale drain in auto-resolve; this title's list has neither. The earlier pass held this same file (same hash) and called it names-only; these descriptions were in it.

verdicts.how: Same re-fetched schema_troy.ron and own parser as data-01. All nine quoted pairs occur verbatim once; campaign_bonus_value_battle_context_specifiers_tables (key, night_battles_only Boolean) confirmed at line 63906. Night-setup texts compared with WARHAMMER II, the THREE KINGDOMS and WARHAMMER III schemas (fetched by the checker; hashes in targeted-05).
verdicts.note: The definitions are real and every listed term is conditional, which supports the Q1 point. The night-setup reading is not supported by this title's own text. Its attacker key has a description rewritten in this title only: 'Fatigue penalty for units during autoresolve night battles'. 3K and WH3 read 'Fatigue penalty for all attackers in a night battle'; WH2 reads 'Morale bonus for units defending night battles'. The defender-morale key's text here is 'Fatigue penalty for all attackers in a night battle.' So 'a fatigue penalty for the attackers and a morale bonus for the defenders' rests on key names against both descriptions. It also drops the 'autoresolve' limit, which may confine the attacker penalty to auto-resolved battles. That 'Surprised' is the ambushed side's term stays INFERRED; no key names an ambush or a detection.

verdicts.how: Same re-fetched schema_troy.ron and own parser as data-01. campaign_variables lookup (line 158283) holds 1,138 pairs. 36 keys start with 'military_force_morale', all tagged '(IN GAME)', each with the same text in WARHAMMER II (36/36). The family is also in WARHAMMER III (36) and THREE KINGDOMS (35). Exactly 2 variables are tagged '(UNUSED)'. campaign_group_morale_effects_tables (effect_bundle, group, key, name) is at line 69322.
verdicts.note: Matches the claim, including 'use NOT established'. The '(IN GAME)' tag is weak evidence of use: it also marks the Waaagh keys, 'influence_threshold_percentage_rebellion' ('Outdated. Currenrlt, influence does not impact rebellions.') and 'influence_threshold_percentage_medium' ('No effect.'). No key in the family charges morale for fighting a battle as such.

verdicts.note: THREE KINGDOMS and WARHAMMER III both define cai_task_management_system_variables_tables. 3K's holds all 10 of this title's keys, and both 'level of a forces morale ... Range: 0.0-1.0' thresholds read identically in both titles. So the table is absent only from WH2. It is inherited from the 2019 sibling's campaign AI, not 'found only in this title's schema', and not 'configured for this title rather than only inherited' (the claim's notes). verdicts.how: Same re-fetched schema_troy.ron and own parser as data-01. The quotes are verbatim; both weighting descriptions are identical and name one effect, UME_CONCERNED_FRIENDS_ROUTING.
verdicts.note: The friendly half is supported at definition level: a 'concerned' effect fed by the rout balance within front and flank distances. verdicts.how: Same re-fetched schema_troy.ron and own parser as data-01. The quotes are verbatim (winning slightly, plain, significantly; losing plain and significantly; blood bonuses at 5, 7.5 and 12 %; charge_bonus and charge_timeout; the army-destruction ratios; max_reinforcement_bonus).
verdicts.note: Caveat: 'No key names the battle's overall balance otherwise' leaves out 'enemy_control_land_defender_land_force_strength_modifier', in the same list. It is applied 'before comparing to attacker strength as part of the enemy_controls_land evaluation', a side-level strength comparison of unclear use. WARHAMMER III lacks the enemy-numbers multiplier and has explicit 'enemy_morale_penalty_combat_power_*' and '_value_*' keys (relative combat power), which this title lacks.

contradictions: targeted-05 against THREE KINGDOMS and WARHAMMER III schemas (fetched by the checker, SHA-256 f09177fa...a614 and 3766315e...132e): both define cai_task_management_system_variables_tables with the same two 'level of a forces morale' thresholds, identical text. So the table is inherited from the 2019 sibling's AI, not unique to this title or configured for it.

data-02 and data-24 against this title's own descriptions: 'unit_battle_setup_night_battle_attacker_fatigue_penalty' is described here only as 'Fatigue penalty for units during autoresolve night battles' (3K and WH3: 'Fatigue penalty for all attackers in a night battle'; WH2: 'Morale bonus for units defending night battles'). The defender-morale key's text here is 'Fatigue penalty for all attackers in a night battle.' The claims' reading, that attackers start fought night battles fatigued and defenders get a morale bonus, rests on key names against the texts and drops the autoresolve limit.

official-23 (closing generalisation), official-06 (INFERRED note) and official not_found Q2 ('morale exists on the campaign side only as conditional effects, none of them a stock') against: official-18 (Battle Glory, a per-army stock that guides say buffs morale); official-19 and community-06 (Achilles' mood); targeted-01 and targeted-02 (hero motivation, a per-hero stock said to feed the hero's morale); and data-14 (an inherited 36-key military-force morale stock defined in the data, use not established).

community-01 and official not_found Q1 (no source describes a morale cost for entering or being in a battle) against targeted-01 and the community log's own C2/C76. targeted-01 (fan wiki): fighting a battle in his own territory lowers an Adventurer hero's motivation; reinforcing or being reinforced lowers a Competitive hero's; motivation feeds the hero's morale. C2/C76: an unplaced NamuWiki line, 'joining an army as lowering morale by 5%'. Not a direct contradiction (conditional, and a hero stock rather than unit morale), but the flat absence statements need this qualification.

Flank morale. The preview (official-10) and TV Tropes (community-01, community-09) say flanking especially damages or destroys morale. One player says enveloped units 'refuse to route until they are almost destroyed when surrounded' (community-09). A mod author says the flank penalty 'does not work correctly and often applies to frontal combat' (data-22). The data's term is set by first contact ('First contact from flank', data-04), which could produce both reports (INFERRED).

Post-rally window in siblings (community-12). 'In most TW titles, this is in the 10-15 second range' and 'it's 10s in Warhammer2' (Cataph's mod) against C70: a WARHAMMER mod shortens its equivalent from 60 to 45 s, and a ROME II mod sets the timer to 60 s.
official-20: Ares' sword and axe morale bonus is +20% at 'Respected' (fan wiki, S15) against +40% at tier one (PCGamesN, S66).
official-05: the camp follower with the 'all enemy units tired' action is the Disguised Trader in one summary and the Egyptian Healer in another.
community-11: 'Rallying Call' is attributed to Agamemnon (C45) and to Sarpedon (C51); 'False Omen' is listed under Sarpedon (Chinese guide) while the English guide gives 'False Portent' to Odysseus.
official-40: EU4 1.34's daily morale damage is '1% of max morale' (developer diary) against '1% of the average max morale of the enemy's troops' (patch note).

Searches that disagree: S5 did not surface the 1.1.0 'very tired' line that S3 and S13 returned (official-01). S8 and S29 did not find S1's '16 ancillaries and 1 trait' line, but S20 recorded a related one (official-07). S9 and S28 did not find the Oration of Dread line that S1 and S20 returned (official-22). S44, S45 and S48 could not find S42's two developer quotes (official-11, official-12). T10 did not find T5's Peaceful, Servile and Sentry traits (targeted-01). T12 and T17 did not confirm T6's 'Widely Known' (targeted-09). T24 did not return T22's army-destruction function (targeted-08).

Claims against their own logs. official-08 cites S1 and S20 'in both', but S20's entry has neither line. official-09 cites S6 and S52, but S52's entry lacks the line. official-15 cites 'three summaries (S1, S3, S66)', but only S1 has it and the S69 exact-phrase check failed. official not_found says Oration of Dread was 'not confirmed by a second search', though S1 and S20 both returned it. community-01 and community-09 cite 'C3 and C38 (TV Tropes)' and quote 'in particular destroys morale in Troy', but C38 has no TV Tropes content and the log never records that wording.
data-19 against the schema: it says 'eight result grades', but the loyalty_interfaction_battle_result_* keys include a ninth, 'draw'.

data-06 against the schema: 'enemy routs nearby raise it', but both weightings feed one effect named UME_CONCERNED_FRIENDS_ROUTING (a concern), and no 'encouraged' counterpart exists among the 129 morale keys.

Annex A.1 and A.3 of the morale proposal (earlier pass) against data-01: the earlier pass downloaded the same schema_troy.ron (same SHA-256) and called it table and field names only, saying the keys were 'not available'. The same file holds all 129 morale keys with descriptions, so several 'not verified for this game' cells could have been answered at definition level from it.
